target: scripts/7_evo/gpufe/contact.py:106-108 + newton.py:190-192 + solver.py:356 (Coulomb friction stick anchor)
claim: The GPU friction resets the stick anchor of EVERY contact node to its current projection at the start of each load increment. FEBio keeps the original stick point while a point sticks and resets it only after slip. As a result, the elastic tangential offset of a sticking node is forgotten every increment and has to be rebuilt. The cage then creeps by about (shear / tangential contact stiffness) per increment, permanently and in proportion to the number of increments. That is spurious ratcheting in exactly the quantity that decides slip-out (cage-centre translation, ratcheting over 3 cycles). The docstrings claim the GPU code works 'exactly as FESlidingElasticInterface::ContactTraction'; that claim is false.
evidence: GPU: newton.py:192 'if p.kind == sliding and p.mu > 0: p.set_anchor(x)' at every increment for all nodes; contact.py:106-108 set_anchor = current closest point; contact.py:156-158 trial force = k (anchor - slave) -> tangential part 0 at increment start. FEBio 4 source third_party/FEBio/FEBioMech/FESlidingElasticInterface.cpp:136 (m_rsp = m_rs at step start) and :880-881 (while stuck m_rs = m_rsp, i.e. the stick point is kept), :897-903 (only slip moves it). 1D replica of both rules (roles/redteam/r0001_anchor_drift.py): block that must stick (T_max 10 N < mu N 30 N), 3 load-unload cycles: FEBio rule residual 0; GPU rule residual = sum T_n / k = 300 / 600 / 1200 (k = 1) for 10 / 20 / 40 increments per half cycle - grows with refinement. Order of magnitude for the cage (cage is the slave side: case.feb SurfacePair cage_C3 slave = cage_top; auto-penalty eps = 10 E / 0.2 mm; footprint 92.8 mm2; peak face shear ~15 N from r0001_i001): drift per increment 5e-6 mm (hard phi = 1 face) to 4e-4 mm (soft phi = 0 face); 6 directions x 3 cycles x 20 increments -> 0.002 to 0.14 mm. Below the 1 mm limit, but of the order of the ratcheting signal to be recorded, step-size dependent, and design dependent (soft contact faces drift more), so the designer can be ranked by an artefact. Gate 1c cannot see this: it never holds a sticking interface under changing shear across increments (gate1c_report.json: stick rows have zero shear until t 0.5, then forced sliding).
how_to_reproduce: python -I human_study/evo/roles/redteam/r0001_anchor_drift.py; read the cited lines of contact.py / newton.py and FESlidingElasticInterface.cpp.

fix_options.option: Implement the FEBio rule: keep (anchor_tri, anchor_L) for nodes that ended the previous increment in stick; re-anchor only nodes that slipped (anchor = current point) or newly entered contact
fix_options.risk: low; also brings the stick-slip switching closer to FEBio for gate 4

fix_options.option: New gate 1d 'stick memory': block under normal load, tangential load ramped to 0.5 mu N and back, 3 cycles, at 10 / 20 / 40 increments: residual displacement must be ~0 and independent of the increment count; plus a twisted-disc case (spin) and a reversal case
Interim: report cage translation together with its value at halved increment size (the planned gate 5 'loading 2x slower' would expose it if applied to the translation, not only to kinetic energy)

summary_zh: GPU 求解器的摩擦計算有一個與 FEBio 不同的地方。在每個負荷增量開始時，GPU 程式把所有接觸點的「黏著參考點」重設到目前位置；FEBio 則會把仍黏著的點的參考位置保留下來，只有真的滑動後才更新。後果是：本應完全黏住的 cage，每個增量都會多滑一點點，而且卸載後回不來，增量越多滑得越多，等於人為製造出「棘輪式累積滑移」，而這正是判斷 cage 會不會滑出的關鍵量。紅隊的一維模型顯示：依 FEBio 規則，殘餘位移為 0；依 GPU 規則，殘餘位移隨增量數成比例增加。粗略估算，6 個方向各 3 次循環後，cage 會多出 0.002 至 0.14 毫米的假滑移，cage 表面越軟越大。現有的摩擦驗證關卡測不到這個問題。建議改成 FEBio 的做法，並新增「黏著記憶」測試。
